questions.q: What is Neo4j's page cache the direct equivalent of, in relational database terms?
options: A buffer pool — it caches on-disk store pages in memory to avoid repeated disk reads
A transaction log — it records every write for durability
A query optimizer — it decides which execution plan to use
A connection pool — it manages client connections to the database
questions.explain: The page cache caches graph store pages in memory, the same role SQL Server's buffer pool plays for data pages.

questions.q: What does PROFILE actually do when prefixed on a Cypher query, as opposed to EXPLAIN?
options: PROFILE runs the query and returns the actual execution plan with real row counts and db hits; EXPLAIN shows the plan without running the query
PROFILE and EXPLAIN are identical and interchangeable
PROFILE only works on write queries, never on reads
PROFILE deletes the query results after showing the plan
questions.explain: PROFILE is the equivalent of a SQL Server actual execution plan; EXPLAIN is closer to an estimated plan since it doesn't execute the query.

questions.q: In a PROFILE output, what does seeing NodeByLabelScan instead of NodeIndexSeek on a filtered property typically indicate?
options: The query is scanning all nodes of that label instead of using an index seek — the graph equivalent of an unexpected table scan
The query executed successfully with optimal performance
NodeByLabelScan always means the index cannot exist for that label
This output only appears when a query has a syntax error
questions.explain: A label scan considers every node with that label, which is far more expensive than a direct index seek on a supporting property index.

questions.q: What is the real anti-pattern this lesson identifies as the most common cause of a full graph scan?
options: A MATCH with no label and no supporting index on the filtered property, forcing Neo4j to consider every node in the graph
Using too many relationship types in a single query
Running PROFILE on a query, which itself causes a full scan
Storing too many properties on a single node
questions.explain: Without a label, Neo4j can't narrow the search space at all; without an index, even a labeled search still has to filter every matching node.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a perfectly indexed query can still perform poorly under load?
options: If the page cache is undersized relative to the graph, the indexed data still has to be read from disk repeatedly instead of served from memory
Indexes in Neo4j only work correctly during the first hour after creation
PROFILE invalidates any index it touches
Indexed queries always ignore the page cache entirely by design
questions.explain: Good indexing and adequate page cache sizing are both required together — one without the other still leaves performance on the table under real load.
